Finance teams are not slow because their people are slow. They are slow because the tools they use were built for data storage, not data movement.

QuickBooks stores your transactions. NetSuite stores your journal entries. Stripe stores your revenue data. None of them automatically combine that data into the report your CFO needs by 9am Monday.

A finance professional does that manually, every time, following the same steps.

We published a piece this week that maps the four finance workflows where automation delivers the fastest ROI — with actual trigger-action sequences, not vague categories.

The one that surprised me most when I started tracking it: AP straight-through processing. Teams that automate AP report handling 60-70% of invoices without any manual touchpoint. At 20 minutes per invoice for manual processing, that is 40-47 hours per month recovered for a team processing 200 invoices.

The month-end close automation is the bigger unlock — compressing a 5-8 day close to 2-3 days is the kind of change that affects every business decision that depends on current financial data.

If your finance team is spending more time on data movement than analysis, this is worth reading.

twitter_thread: Finance teams are not slow because their people are slow. They are slow because their tools were built for data storage, not data movement. Here are the 4 workflows to automate first:

Workflow 1 — Weekly financial report: Monday 7am, ERP data pulled automatically, variance analysis run, flagged items highlighted, draft emailed to CFO for review. Not for data entry — for judgment on the exceptions. Teams recover 3-5 hours per week per person.

Workflow 2 — Month-end close: last business day triggers data pull across all systems, reconciliations run automatically, unmatched items routed to the right person with context. Benchmark: 5-8 day close compressed to 2-3 days.

Workflow 3 — AP processing: invoice received → line items extracted → matched to PO → within policy = payment scheduled automatically → variance or no PO = routed to approver. 60-70% of invoices process without any manual touchpoint.

Workflow 4 — Cash flow forecasting: every Friday, AR aging + AP schedule + bank balance pulled, historical payment patterns applied, 30/60/90 day projection posted to Slack. CFO makes decisions. The data gathering happens automatically.

What AI cannot replace in finance: accounting treatment decisions on unusual transactions, audit relationships, and strategic financial planning. AI handles the data movement. Finance professionals handle the judgment.
